title: Fainting and unresponsiveness — breathing normally
spoken_title: someone who has fainted or is not responding
confirm_prompt: This sounds like a faint. Is the person unresponsive but still breathing? Say go, or tap Continue, and I'll talk you through it.

steps.text: Kneel beside them. Say their name loudly and gently squeeze their shoulders. Tell me if they respond.
If they do not respond, tilt their head back gently with one hand on the forehead and two fingertips under the chin. This opens the airway.
Look along their chest and listen at their mouth for up to ten seconds. Are they breathing normally? Occasional gasps are not normal breathing.
If they are breathing normally, roll them onto their side. Keep their head tilted back so the airway stays open and anything in the mouth can drain.
Call for help now if you have not already. Then loosen anything tight around their neck and keep them warm.
Stay with them and keep watching that they are still breathing. Do not leave them alone.
If their breathing stops or starts to sound abnormal, tell me straight away and start chest compressions if you know how.

sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020 — Unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing
International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation (ILCOR), Consensus on Science with Treatment Recommendations — Recovery position
